name: Lanluma

card.summary: An injectable poly-L-lactic acid collagen stimulator, used by clinicians to rebuild volume and firmness in the face and body gradually over sessions.
card.note: Clinic-administered injectable; lumps and nodules are the most reported side effects, and rare vascular events are described.

quick.overview:
Lanluma is an injectable made of poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), a collagen stimulator in the same family as Sculptra. Practitioners use it to restore volume and skin support in the face, neck, hands, arms, thighs and decollete, with results that build over weeks as the body lays down collagen rather than appearing at once.

Published work includes a 9-month multicenter post-market observational study across five body areas and small retrospective case series on facial and scalp-based lifting.
quick.how: It is a clinician-administered injection, delivered in a series of sessions weeks apart, with results developing gradually. Technique details belong to trained practitioners and are not covered here.
quick.risks: In the post-market study, lumps and nodules were the most frequent adverse events, all treatment-related and none serious, and none were reported in the decollete. A case report describes PLLA-related vascular events treated with ultrasound-guided hyaluronidase. It is a prescription-level procedure that should be performed by qualified clinicians.

lead: Lanluma is a poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) collagen stimulator injected by clinicians to improve volume, contour and skin firmness. It is described as similar to Sculptra. [1][2]

PLLA stimulates collagen: Wikipedia explains that it provokes a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release mediators such as TGF-beta, prompting fibroblasts to deposit collagen. [4] A 2024 post-market study followed 70 participants and 99 treatment sessions of the neck, upper arm, hand, thigh and decollete for 9 months. [1]

A 2025 retrospective review of 12 patients treated with Lanluma V on the scalp for combined forehead and temporal lifting reported an average 1.16-grade improvement on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale at 6 months and no non-scarring alopecia. [2]

paras: Lanluma V contains 210 mg PLLA and is distributed by Sinclair Pharmaceutical, according to a 2025 clinical paper. [2] It acts by stimulating collagen regeneration to support the treated area. [2]
In the 9-month study, lumps (neck, upper arm, hand) and nodules (neck, hand, thigh) were the most frequent adverse events; none were serious, severe or fatal. [1]
A case series described one PLLA and two calcium hydroxylapatite vascular events resolved without necrosis or scarring using ultrasound-guided hyaluronidase. [3]

A multicenter, open-label, uncontrolled post-market study followed 70 participants for 9 months. [1] A retrospective series of 12 patients rated at 6 months showed improvement on the GAIS. [2] Both are uncontrolled designs.

timeline.event: Post-market study begins with first injections in September. [1]
